description: Optional Anyshift resource and relationship synchronization for the Backstage catalog
name: @anyshift/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-anyshift
readme:
# `@anyshift/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-anyshift`

Optional catalog module for synchronizing Anyshift infrastructure Resources and runtime relations.
GitHub remains authoritative for Components and ownership. The module never creates or replaces a
Component.

```ts
backend.add(
  import('@anyshift/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-anyshift'),
);
```

Use `anyshift.catalog.mode: shadow` before enabling `active` synchronization. Matching prioritizes
`anyshift.io/target` and falls back to the repository name from `github.com/project-slug`. See the
[integration guide](../../README.md) for the ownership and failure-handling contract.

Projects whose graph inventory is not Kubernetes-based should configure `inventoryTypes` explicitly.
Use `resourceNamePatterns` to scope generated Resources and `activeTargets` to roll out Component
enrichment through a reviewed, non-empty allowlist. Omit `activeTargets` only when every matched
Component is intentionally eligible. Generated cloud Resources are type-prefixed, include a stable
graph-identity suffix when available, and carry `anyshift.io/managed-by: catalog-provider`.
AWS ARN-backed Resources also carry provider, account, region, and ARN annotations plus a
read-only AWS Console link. Lambda functions are exposed as workloads, S3 buckets as datastores,
and SQS queues as topics so their entity-specific Anyshift content is available.

In active mode the module persists the latest reconciliation outcome as
`resource:default/anyshift-catalog-sync`. It also mounts
`POST /api/catalog/anyshift/reconcile`; callers need an authenticated Backstage user identity and
the `anyshift.catalog.sync` permission. Concurrent scheduled and manual requests are coalesced into
one provider run.
